newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RUGBY UNION-ARGENTINA INCLUDE FIRST PROFESSIONAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ARGENTINA INCLUDE FIRST PROFESSIONAL.

text.p: Hooker Federico Mendez, Argentina's first professional, has been included in the national side to meet South Africa in the first of two tests on Saturday.
Mendez, who played for Natal this season, has signed to play for English club champions Bath next year.
World champions South Africa have played four tests against Argentina and will be defending an unbeaten record at the Ferrocarril Oeste Stadium.
Three years ago in the corresponding match the Pumas came closest to upsetting the Springboks with a brilliant second half display which brought them to within three points at 26-29.
Only three Springboks remain from that side, wings James Small and Jacques Olivier and flanker Ruben Kruger, but the management is not underestimating the threat posed by the Pumas.

"Everyone is talking about us being professional now and the Pumas still being amateur, and of course that's true. But in some ways it has brought the Argentinian players even closer together," said coach Andre Markgraaff.
"They were always a passionate side, but now they feel they have the odds stacked against them. They can fall back on the idea that you play with your heart for your country.

"The Pumas have abandoned the mauling game they used in the World Cup and have adapted well to the new laws. Our biggest mistake would be not to take them seriously just because they are still amateurs in the old sense of the word."

South Africa's players are struggling to come to terms with the new ideas Markgraaff and his management team are trying to adopt. On Tuesday in Rosario the midweek side played the new game for 23 minutes and scored five tries, but then lost control ofthe ball and nearly lost the game in the closing minutes.

Assistant coach Nick Mallett said: "What we are trying to do is inject pace into the game, securing the ball on the ground and popping it up for the forwards to drive on to before releasing the backs, the same way that Natal play.

"On Tuesday the guys did that well until they forgot that you have to slow the game down at times in order to give your own players a chance to recover. That means not tapping every penalty, but kicking for touch occasionally, winning the lineouts and then starting again from the subsequent maul."
The Springboks have only one area of apparent weakness; in the front row where Dawie Theron and James Dalton may struggle against Roberto Grau and Mendez.
But elsewhere they have pace aplenty and if they can control the ball in the manner espoused by their management their unbeaten run against the Pumas should not be under threat.

Argentina - 15-Facundo Soler; 14-Octavio Bartolucci, 13-Gonzalo Camardon, 12-Lisandro Arbizu, 11-Tomas Solari; 10-Jose Luis Cilley, 9-Nicolas Fernandez Miranda; 8-Pablo Jose Caemerlinckx, 7-Raul Perez, 6-Rolando Martin, 5-Pedro Sporleder, 4-German Llans, 3-Omar Hasan Jalil, 2-Federico Mendez, 1-Roberto Grau.

South Africa - 15-Andre Joubert, 14-James Small, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Hennie Le Roux, 11-Jacques Olivier; 10-Henry Honiball, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann, 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Kobus Wiese, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-James Dalton, 1-Dawie Theron.
